expectations.text: Output does NOT simply accept the simplified model and move to write-up guidance
expectations.evidence: The response opens with 'Before writing this up, I'd push back on the model you landed on — there's a real risk it's anti-conservative for your condition test' and spends the bulk of the response diagnosing and fixing the model before any write-up guidance.

expectations.text: Output raises that dropping random slopes to fix convergence risks under-specifying the model and inflating Type I error
expectations.evidence: 'When you drop the slope and use only a random intercept, the residual variance absorbs the between-subject variability in the condition effect — this deflates your standard error and makes the test anti-conservative. Type I error rates in this situation routinely run 2–5× the nominal rate (Barr et al., 2013; Schielzeth & Forstmeier, 2009).'

expectations.text: Output names at least one upstream fix that should be tried before dropping slopes — predictor scaling, sum coding, allFit() / alternative optimizers, or dropping correlation parameters with || before dropping slopes
expectations.evidence: The response names multiple upstream fixes: Fix 1 uses allFit() to sweep optimizers, Fix 2 covers sum/±0.5 coding and scaling, Fix 3 introduces the zero-correlation model as a principled intermediate before fully dropping slopes.

expectations.text: Output recommends inspecting the random-effects variance components to diagnose which component is at the boundary — e.g. VarCorr(), summary()$varcor, rePCA(), or equivalent — rather than simplifying by trial and error
expectations.evidence: 'check *what* is singular before simplifying' followed by explicit code: `VarCorr(m_max)   # which variance component is at/near zero?`

expectations.text: Output notes that the condition slope is missing from a within-subjects design and this is the most consequential omission — not just a minor simplification
expectations.evidence: Under 'The problem with your current model': 'Your condition manipulation is within-subjects... The correct error term for testing a within-subjects effect requires a by-subject random slope for condition.' The section heading and the anti-conservative framing clearly mark this as the most consequential issue, not a minor detail.
